stakeholder_audit.content: When color (or other semantic properties like size/alpha) is mapped from boolean data, should Plot treat True/False as two discrete categories (i.e., use a Nominal/categorical scale, like strings) rather than a numeric/continuous scale? This would give a qualitative palette with one color per boolean value instead of a continuous gradient.

Not for this issue. In numeric contexts, boolean values should be upcast like numpy/matplotlib: False -> 0.0 and True -> 1.0. So a continuous/interval scale should not fail and should map them as 0/1. Broader boolean semantic scale behavior can be revisited separately.

The agent describes the behavior change it made or intends to make. Say whether it matches what you asked for and which requirement still seems unmet, in your own words; do not name code.
so.Plot(['a','b'], [1,2], color=[True, False]).add(so.Bar()) now plots without error. Internally, when a Continuous/interval scale (used by default for color, size, etc.) encounters boolean data, the booleans are upcast to floats (False->0.0, True->1.0) before doing any numeric scale math, matching numpy/matplotlib's normal bool-to-float upcasting. I verified this also works for boolean data used as x/y coordinates, boolean size mapping, and when a Continuous scale is explicitly requested for boolean data. The full test suite for scales/properties/plot still passes.

Yes, that matches what I asked for: boolean data in numeric/continuous contexts should not raise, and should behave as 0/1 floats with False -> 0 and True -> 1. I don’t see an unmet requirement in that description.
